cells.tense: The feeling is resting here and nothing is being forced into an answer.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Follow whatever you face next in thought until it stops making sense, then stop there. Ten minutes is plenty, and stopping at the edge counts as done.
cells.core:
Something in you already holds the shape of this without needing to say it. You can move a step at a time while the rest stays unclear, and that has been enough so far. None of it has to be turned into an answer to be trusted.

When the next thing keeps shifting, give it more room rather than less. Follow one line of it in your head until it reaches the point where it gives out, and stop at that point. No one has to see the far end to go as far as the thing actually goes. The feeling is doing its own work; this only lets your thinking catch up to it. The place where it gives out is a real place, and knowing where it is tells you something.
cells.sheetLine: Trust the step within reach, and nothing beyond it.
cells.handle: …knowing where it is tells you something.
cells.verb: Sitting with what the heart already knows before deciding anything
cells.place: Where only the next step shows and nothing past it does

cells.tense: The mind keeps running ahead to a place it cannot write its way into.
cells.ask: Take one ending that has already finished and gather what it gave you — three things, no more — then close the page and stop counting.
cells.core:
You have been living in what happens next — sorting it, bracing for it, working it out before it arrives. The feeling that used to rest is being spent on a future nobody can hand you. The road only shows one step, and looking harder does not widen it.

An ending has already run its course somewhere near this. Before you plan the next move, gather what that one grew: what it gave and what it took, three items, no lesson attached. What is already over will do more for the step ahead than anything you rehearse about tomorrow. You are not behind. You are standing in material you have not yet collected, and it is waiting there.

cells.tense: The quiet came and the present is still being met from behind it.
cells.act: reconcile what you know with what you feel about it
cells.ask: Put one thing you are stuck on into two lists — what you know and what you sense — then take a single step out of either side.
cells.core:
What used to settle by itself has gone still, and you are working from behind the moment instead of inside it. Ideas arrive, but they will not gather. The next step stays foggy longer than it should. This is not a failure of feeling — it is a tank that has run low, and it can be refilled.

Do not push for feeling; that drains the wrong one. Instead, take whatever you keep circling and put it into two lists — what you know for certain and what you sense underneath — then do the next move that comes out of either side. The move can be tiny. When your thinking has a shape again, the quiet returns by itself, and steps start showing themselves instead of fog.

cells.tense: Something in you is already reading the situation while the official account says you are just waiting.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Go through the hardest piece of what you are sitting with twice, slowly, before you set it down for the day — no notes, no conclusions drawn.
cells.core:
What other people call patience in you is doing real work. You settle, you let things breathe, and underneath you are already working the shape of it out — but when asked how you know, you say you are waiting to see. The depth is running the show, and the waiting gets the credit.

There is a simpler version, and it is closer to where you already are. Pick the hardest piece of what you are sitting with and go through it twice, slowly, before you set it down — no notes, no conclusions drawn. Then leave it for the day. That is not waiting. That is the thing you do, and it will keep working whether or not you put your name on it.
